pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


When you first start following Jesus, you hear a lot of stories. You hear about Noah and the ark. You hear about Moses and the Red Sea. You hear about David and Goliath. You hear about Jonah and the big fish. They are exciting stories. They are famous stories. They are Sunday school stories.


But then you might wonder, "What do these stories have to do with me? What do they have to do with Jesus? Are they just ancient history?" The answer is no. They are not just ancient history. They are not just Sunday school stories. They are more than just stories. They are clues. They are patterns. They are blueprints. And every single one of them points to Jesus.


This book is for you. You are new to the faith. You are building your foundation. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 Old Testament heroes. We are going to see their stories. We are going to see their lives. And we are going to see how they point to Jesus. They are more than just stories. They are the story of your Savior.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Old Testament as just a collection of old stories. You will see it as a gallery of heroes. You will see it as a pattern. You will see it as a blueprint. You will understand the Old Testament heroes. You will understand their stories. You will understand why they matter for your new life. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for your Bible. And you will have a new appreciation for the one who is the fulfillment of every story.


How to Use This Guide

pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, even though he did not know where he was going." - Hebrews 11:8 (Written around 60 A.D.)


Abraham had faith. He trusted God. He obeyed. He went. He did not know where he was going. He did not know what would happen. But he trusted God. He had faith. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich." - 2 Corinthians 8:9


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham left his home. Jesus left heaven. Abraham went to a land he did not know. Jesus came to a world he created. Abraham trusted God. Jesus trusted the Father. Abraham was a hero of faith. Jesus is the ultimate hero of faith.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might be stepping out in faith. You might be leaving something behind. You might be trusting God for something you cannot see. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus took the greatest step of faith. He left heaven for you. He trusts the Father. You can trust Him.


Faith Builder
Think of a step of faith you need to take. Write it down. Ask God to help you take it. Thank Jesus for taking the greatest step of faith for you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his faith. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He left heaven for me. Help me to step out in faith. Help me to trust you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Then God said, 'Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you.'" - Genesis 22:2 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God tested Abraham. He asked him to sacrifice his son. His only son. The son he loved. Abraham was willing. He was willing to give up everything. He was willing to sacrifice. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life." - John 3:16


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham was willing to sacrifice his son. God actually sacrificed His Son. Abraham was willing to give up his only son. God gave up His only Son. Abraham was a hero of sacrifice. Jesus is the ultimate hero of sacrifice.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a sacrifice. You might need someone to give everything for you. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus gave everything for you. He gave His life. He gave His love. You are the reason for His sacrifice.


Faith Builder
Think of something you can sacrifice for someone else this week. It does not have to be big. It could be your time. It could be your money. It could be your comfort. Ask God to help you do it.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his willingness to sacrifice. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that you gave your only Son for me. Help me to sacrifice for others. Help me to give generously. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Promise (OT)
"I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing." - Genesis 12:2 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God made a promise to Abraham. He promised him a great nation. He promised him a great name. He promised him a blessing. Abraham waited. He trusted. He believed. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham..." - Matthew 1:1


Jesus is the fulfillment of the promise. He is the descendant of Abraham. He is the great nation. He is the great name. He is the blessing. Abraham waited for the promise. Jesus is the promise. He is the ultimate hero of the promise.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might be waiting for a promise. You might be waiting for God to do something. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the fulfillment of every promise. He is the hope. He is the future. He is the blessing. You can trust His promises.


Faith Builder
Write down one promise from God that you are holding onto. Say it out loud. Thank God for keeping His promises.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his patience. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the fulfillment of every promise. Help me to trust your promises. Help me to wait for them. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Promise (OT)
"Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, 'Abraham!' 'Here I am,' he replied." - Genesis 22:1 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God tested Abraham. He tested his faith. He tested his trust. He tested his obedience. Abraham passed the test. He passed the trial. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"For we do not have a high priest who is unable to empathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who has been tempted in every way, just as we are—yet he did not sin." - Hebrews 4:15


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham was tested and passed. Jesus was tempted and did not sin. Abraham was tried. Jesus was tried. Abraham was a hero of the test. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the test.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might be tested. You might be tried. You might be put through a trial. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus passed every test. He passed every trial. He can help you pass yours.


Faith Builder
Think of a test you are facing. Write it down. Ask God to help you pass it. Thank Jesus for passing every test for you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his faith in the test. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He passed every test for me. Help me to pass my tests. Help me to trust you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Promise (OT)
"On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided." - Genesis 22:14 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham went to the mountain. He went to Moriah. He went to the place where God would provide. He called the place "The LORD Will Provide." He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus." - Philippians 4:19


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham went to the mountain of provision. Jesus went to the mountain of the cross. Abraham saw God provide a ram. Jesus became the lamb. Abraham was a hero of the mountain. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the mountain.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have a mountain in your life. You might have a high place. You might have a challenge. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus went to the mountain of the cross for you. He provided the sacrifice. He provided the lamb.


Faith Builder
Think of a mountain you are facing. Write it down. Ask God to help you climb it. Thank Jesus for going to the mountain of the cross for you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the mountain of provision. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He went to the cross for me. Help me to trust your provision. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Promise (OT)
"So Abram went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he pitched his tents. There he built an altar to the LORD." - Genesis 13:18 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham built an altar. He built a place to worship. He built a place to sacrifice. He built a place to meet with God. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"We have an altar from which those who minister at the tabernacle have no right to eat." - Hebrews 13:10


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham built an altar. Jesus is the altar. Abraham sacrificed on the altar. Jesus sacrificed himself on the altar. Abraham was a hero of the altar. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the altar.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need an altar. You might need a place to meet with God. You might need a place to sacrifice. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the altar. He is the place where you can meet God. He is the place where you can sacrifice.


Faith Builder
Find a quiet place to meet with God. It could be your room. It could be a park. It could be your car. Spend five minutes there with God. Thank Jesus for being the altar.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the altar. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the altar. Help me to meet with you. Help me to worship you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Promise (OT)
"He took him outside and said, 'Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.' Then he said to him, 'So shall your offspring be.'" - Genesis 15:5 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God told Abraham to look at the stars. He told him to count them. He told him his offspring would be like the stars. Abraham believed. He trusted. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise." - Galatians 3:29


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham's descendants are like the stars. Jesus made it possible for us to be Abraham's descendants. We are the stars. We are the offspring. Abraham was a hero of the stars. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the stars.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might feel like a nobody. You might feel like a no one. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. You are a star. You are a child of Abraham. You are part of the promise. You are part of the family.


Faith Builder
Go outside tonight. Look at the stars. Count as many as you can. As you look at them, remember that you are a child of Abraham. You are part of the promise.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the stars. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that I am a child of Abraham. Thank you that I am part of the promise. Help me to shine like a star. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Promise (OT)
"Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness." - Genesis 15:6 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham believed God. He trusted God. He had faith. And God credited it to him as righteousness. Abraham was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"However, to the one who does not work but trusts God who justifies the ungodly, their faith is credited as righteousness." - Romans 4:5


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham believed God. We believe in Jesus. Abraham's faith was credited as righteousness. Our faith in Jesus is credited as righteousness. Abraham was a hero of faith. Jesus is the ultimate hero of faith.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might think you have to earn God's love. You might think you have to be good enough. You might think you have to work for it. Remember Abraham. He believed. That was enough. Your faith in Jesus is enough. It is credited to you as righteousness.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "I am made righteous by faith in Jesus, not by my works." Say it out loud. Thank God for this gift.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his faith. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that my faith in Him makes me righteous. Help me to believe. Help me to trust. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his trust. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the lamb. Thank you that He takes away the sin of the world. Help me to trust you. Help me to rely on you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The Hero of the Test of Trust Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"So Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. And to this day it is said, 'On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.'" - Genesis 22:14 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham saw God's provision. He saw the ram. He saw the lamb. He called the place "The LORD Will Provide." He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus." - Philippians 4:19


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham saw the provision. Jesus is the provision. Abraham called the place "The LORD Will Provide." Jesus is the Lord who provides. Abraham was a hero of provision. Jesus is the ultimate hero of provision.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have needs. You might have worries. You might have fears. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the provision. He meets your needs. He takes care of you. He provides for you.


Faith Builder
Think of a need you have. Write it down. Ask God to provide. Thank Him for being your provider.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the provision. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He meets my needs. Thank you that He provides for me. Help me to trust your provision. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: The Hero of the Test of Provision Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Then God said, 'Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you.'" - Genesis 22:2 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God tested Abraham. He tested his son. He tested his child. He tested his family. Abraham passed the test. He was willing to give up his son. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life." - John 3:16


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham was willing to give up his son. God gave up His Son. Abraham was tested with his son. God gave His Son. Abraham was a hero of the son. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the son.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a son. You might need a child. You might need a family. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the Son. He is the child. He is the family. He is the one who was given for you.


Faith Builder
Think about your family. Write down one way you can show them love this week. Ask God to help you do it.
……
pages.title: Day 22: The Hero of the Test of the Son Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the test of the son. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that you gave your only Son for me. Help me to trust your love. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: The Hero of the Test of the Son Again (Continued)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"So Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. And to this day it is said, 'On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.'" - Genesis 22:14 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham went to the mountain. He went to Moriah. He went to the place where God would provide. He called the place "The LORD Will Provide." He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit." - 1 Peter 3:18


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham went to the mountain. Jesus went to the cross. Abraham went to the place of provision. Jesus became the provision. Abraham was a hero of the mountain. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the mountain.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have a mountain. You might have a high place. You might have a challenge. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus went to the mountain of the cross for you. He provided the sacrifice. He provided the lamb.


Faith Builder
Draw a picture of a mountain. Write the word "Jesus" at the top. Thank Him for going to the mountain of the cross for you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the mountain. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He went to the cross for me. Help me to trust your provision. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: The Hero of the Test of the Mountain Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"So Abram went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he pitched his tents. There he built an altar to the LORD." - Genesis 13:18 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham built an altar. He built a place of worship. He built a place of sacrifice. He built a place to meet with God. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"We have an altar from which those who minister at the tabernacle have no right to eat." - Hebrews 13:10


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham built an altar. Jesus is the altar. Abraham sacrificed on the altar. Jesus sacrificed himself on the altar. Abraham was a hero of the altar. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the altar.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need an altar. You might need a place to meet with God. You might need a place to sacrifice. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the altar. He is the place where you can meet God. He is the place where you can sacrifice.


Faith Builder
Find a quiet place to meet with God. Spend five minutes there with Him. Thank Jesus for being the altar.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the altar. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the altar. Help me to meet with you. Help me to worship you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: The Hero of the Test of the Altar Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram and said, 'To your descendants I give this land...'" - Genesis 15:18 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God made a covenant with Abraham. He made an agreement. He made a promise. He said, "To your descendants I give this land." Abraham was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"For this reason Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance..." - Hebrews 9:15


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham received a covenant. Jesus is the mediator of the new covenant. Abraham received the promise of land. Jesus received the promise of eternal life. Abraham was a hero of the covenant. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the covenant.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a covenant. You might need an agreement. You might need a promise. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the mediator of the new covenant. He made a promise with you. He made an agreement with you. He made a covenant with you.


Faith Builder
Write down one promise from the new covenant. Say it out loud. Thank Jesus for making a new covenant with you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the covenant. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the mediator of the new covenant. Help me to live in the new covenant. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: The Hero of the Test of the Covenant Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"He took him outside and said, 'Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.' Then he said to him, 'So shall your offspring be.'" - Genesis 15:5 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God told Abraham to look at the stars. He told him to count them. He told him his offspring would be like the stars. Abraham believed. He trusted. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise." - Galatians 3:29


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham's descendants are like the stars. Jesus made it possible for us to be Abraham's descendants. We are the stars. We are the offspring. Abraham was a hero of the stars. Jesus is the ultimate hero of the stars.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might feel like a nobody. You might feel like a no one. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. You are a star. You are a child of Abraham. You are part of the promise. You are part of the family.


Faith Builder
Go outside tonight. Look at the stars. Count as many as you can. Remember that you are a child of Abraham. You are part of the promise.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the stars. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that I am a child of Abraham. Thank you that I am part of the promise. Help me to shine like a star. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The Hero of the Test of the Stars Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness." - Genesis 15:6 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham believed God. He trusted God. He had faith. And God credited it to him as righteousness. Abraham was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"However, to the one who does not work but trusts God who justifies the ungodly, their faith is credited as righteousness." - Romans 4:5


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham believed God. We believe in Jesus. Abraham's faith was credited as righteousness. Our faith in Jesus is credited as righteousness. Abraham was a hero of faith. Jesus is the ultimate hero of faith.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might think you have to earn God's love. You might think you have to be good enough. You might think you have to work for it. Remember Abraham. He believed. That was enough. Your faith in Jesus is enough. It is credited to you as righteousness.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "I am made righteous by faith in Jesus, not by my works." Say it out loud. Thank God for this gift.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his faith. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that my faith in Him makes me righteous. Help me to believe. Help me to trust. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: The Hero of the Test of Faith Again and Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Early the next morning Abraham got up and loaded his donkey. He took with him two of his servants and his son Isaac." - Genesis 22:3 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham obeyed. He got up early. He loaded his donkey. He took his servants. He took his son. He went. He obeyed. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"And being found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to death—even death on a cross!" - Philippians 2:8


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham obeyed God. Jesus obeyed the Father. Abraham went to the mountain. Jesus went to the cross. Abraham was a hero of obedience. Jesus is the ultimate hero of obedience.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to obey. You might need to follow. You might need to trust. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus obeyed the Father for you. He went to the cross for you. He showed you the ultimate obedience.


Faith Builder
Think of one command of Jesus you can obey today. Write it down. Ask God to help you obey it.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his obedience. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He obeyed the Father for me. Help me to obey you. Help me to follow you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: The Hero of the Test of Obedience Again and Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Abraham answered, 'God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.'" - Genesis 22:8 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham trusted God. He trusted God to provide. He trusted God to take care of it. He trusted God to provide the lamb. He was a hero.


The Proof (NT)
"The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, 'Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!'" - John 1:29


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham trusted God to provide a lamb. God provided Jesus. Abraham trusted in the provision. Jesus is the provision. Abraham was a hero of trust. Jesus is the ultimate hero of trust.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to trust. You might need to rely on God. You might need to depend on Him. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the provision. He is the lamb. He is the one who takes away the sin of the world. You can trust Him.


Faith Builder
Think of one thing you are trusting God for. Write it down. Thank Jesus for being the provision.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his trust. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the lamb. Thank you that He takes away the sin of the world. Help me to trust you. Help me to rely on you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The Hero of the Test of Trust Again and Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness." - Genesis 15:6 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham believed God. He trusted God. He had faith. And God credited it to him as righteousness. Abraham was a hero. But he was not the ultimate hero. He pointed to a greater hero. He pointed to Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the ultimate hero. He is the one who came to seek. He is the one who came to save. He is the one who came to rescue. He is the fulfillment of Abraham. He is the ultimate hero.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a hero. You might need a rescue. You might need a savior. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the ultimate hero. He came to seek. He came to save. He came to rescue. You can trust the ultimate hero.


Faith Builder
Write down one thing you have learned about the ultimate hero over the last 30 days. Thank God for the ultimate hero. Thank Him for Jesus.


The Prayer
God, thank you for Abraham. Thank you for the heroes of the faith. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for the ultimate hero. Help me to trust the hero. Help me to follow the hero. Help me to live in the rescue of the hero. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Story Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 days of Old Testament heroes. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It will show you how Jesus is the fulfillment of every hero. As you read, look for the pattern. Look for the clues. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The stories are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The stories point to a person. The stories point to Jesus. You can understand the stories and still miss the Savior. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The stories are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. loves helping new believers build a strong foundation. He believes that faith is not a blind leap. It is a confident step based on evidence. He lives with his family and enjoys hiking and reading.


Coming Next: The Real Hero
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Real Hero takes a 30 day look at how the lives of Joseph, Moses, and David reveal your Savior. It is for the new believer who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of believers. The journey is not over. The adventure is just beginning.

Moses. David. They are all smiling. They are all pointing to a cross in the center. The title MORE THAN JUST STORIES is in a strong, trustworthy, bold serif font. The subtitle is in a gentle, welcoming sans-serif. The overall feel is warm, inviting, and full of hope.
